solutionSketch: The angle inscribed in a semicircle is a right angle (Thales’ theorem on the circle).

solutionSketch: Radius is half the diameter: 14/2 = 7 cm.

questions.stem: ABC is isosceles with principal vertex A and AB = AC. If angle BAC = 40°, then angle ABC equals:
solutionSketch: Base angles are equal: (180° − 40°)/2 = 70°.

solutionSketch: Thales: a parallel to one side cuts the other two sides proportionally.

questions.stem: O is the center of a circle of radius 5. Chord [CD] has length 8. The distance from O to [CD] is:
solutionSketch: The perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord: half-chord = 4.
Distance = √(5² − 4²) = 3.

solutionSketch: The altitude from the principal vertex is also a median: BI = 5.

questions.stem: In triangle ABC, (AI) is the perpendicular bisector of [BC]. Then:
solutionSketch: Any point of the perpendicular bisector of [BC] is equidistant from B and C, so AB = AC.

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C. The altitude from C meets [AB] at H. Then triangles ACH and ABC are similar because:
choices: they share angle A, and both are right-angled
questions.answer: they share angle A, and both are right-angled
solutionSketch: AA criterion: both right-angled, and they share angle A.
This is the usual geometric-mean setup of Brevet sessions.

questions.stem: The midline of triangle ABC joining the midpoints of [AB] and [AC]:
choices: equals BC and is parallel to (BC)
is parallel to (BC) and equal to BC/2
questions.answer: is parallel to (BC) and equal to BC/2
solutionSketch: Midline (mid-segment) theorem: parallel to the third side and half as long.

questions.stem: M is the image of A by the translation of vector BC. Quadrilateral ABCM is:
solutionSketch: AM = BC (equal and parallel), so ABCM is a parallelogram.
It is a rectangle or rhombus only with extra hypotheses.

solutionSketch: A translation maps a line to a parallel line (the same line if the vector is parallel to it).

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C, AC = 8, BC = 6. Then tan of angle A equals:
solutionSketch: Opposite to A is BC = 6, adjacent is AC = 8, so tan A = 6/8 = 3/4.
Trap: 4/3 (that is tan B) or using the hypotenuse.

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C with AB = 10 and AC = 6. Then sin of angle B equals:
solutionSketch: BC = 8. Opposite to B is AC = 6, hypotenuse 10, so sin B = 6/10 = 3/5.

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C with AC = 6 and BC = 8. The radius of the circle circumscribed about triangle ABC is:
solutionSketch: In a right triangle the circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse.
AB = 10, so R = 5. Trap: taking R = AB = 10.

questions.stem: From a point P outside a circle, a tangent [PT] and a secant through A then B are drawn, with PA = 4 and PB = 9. Then PT equals:
solutionSketch: Power of a point: PT² = PA × PB = 36, so PT = 6.
Trap: adding 4+9 or taking √(9−4).

solutionSketch: A rectangle is cyclic; the diagonal is a diameter: AC = 10, radius 5.

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C, AB = 13, AC = 5, BC = 12. The altitude from C to [AB] has length:
solutionSketch: Area two ways: (AC·BC)/2 = (AB·CH)/2, so CH = (5×12)/13 = 60/13.
Trap: taking CH as a geometric mean without the product over AB.

questions.stem: ABC is right-angled at C. H is the foot of the altitude from C to [AB]. Then AH × AB equals:
solutionSketch: Geometric mean: AC² = AH × AB (leg is the geometric mean of hypotenuse and adjacent projection).

questions.stem: In the plane, A(1 ; 2) and vector BC = (4 ; −1). The image of A by the translation of vector BC is:
solutionSketch: Image = (1+4 ; 2+(−1)) = (5 ; 1). Trap: writing the vector itself as the image.
